candidates.name: Maya Chen
candidates.headline: Staff platform lead at a freight marketplace; has already built most of what this role asks for.

must_have.rationale: Every must-have shows up inside a current, dated role with a result attached.
evidence: Lead a 5-person platform team running 3 EKS clusters for 140 services across 2 AWS regions
Moved CI/CD from Jenkins to GitHub Actions and Argo CD
Rolled out OpenTelemetry tracing and Prometheus SLO alerting

experience.rationale: Same work at similar scope (140 vs 180 services, multi-region) for four years, plus SRE time before that.
evidence: Staff Platform Engineer, Parcelly (freight marketplace)

impact.rationale: Several outcomes with baselines that map straight onto the posting's year-one goals.
evidence: deploy lead time went from 2 hours to 18 minutes
pages dropped from 11 to 3 per week
Cut AWS spend 22% ($610K/yr)

learning_agility.rationale: Learned Kubernetes on the job and led the first pilot, then grew into leading a platform team. Recent learning is less visible than early-career learning.
evidence: Learned Kubernetes on the job and ran the bank's first EKS pilot
Built a Terraform module library and Backstage golden paths

work_style.rationale: Ownership tied to outcomes, mentoring with a result, and a process artifact others still use.
evidence: Mentored 3 engineers; two were promoted to senior
wrote the blameless postmortem template still in use

nice_to_have.rationale: Kafka, FinOps, least-privilege IAM, and logistics domain all demonstrated.
evidence: Ran Kafka (MSK) pipelines processing 40M routing events per day
least privilege by default

strengths: Has already hit the posting's year-one targets elsewhere: self-service environments, sub-30-minute deploys, fewer pages
Logistics domain and multi-region EKS at comparable scale
Mentors with a track record of promotions
gaps: Staff title; check level and comp expectations against a senior band
Less hands-on coding evidence in the current role than the last one

interview_questions.question: Walk me through the multi-region failover design at Parcelly. What failed the first time you tested it?
The deploy lead time went from 2 hours to 18 minutes. What were the three biggest contributors, and what did you try that did not help?
When you ran the first EKS pilot at Harbor Bank, how did you get productive on Kubernetes in the first few weeks? What would you do differently now?
Tell me about a time a product team pushed back on a golden path you built. How did it end?
This is a senior IC role with mentoring, not a team lead role. How do you feel about stepping back from managing?

candidates.name: Dev Patel
candidates.headline: Former school-district sysadmin, three years into platform work, with a fast and well-documented ramp.

must_have.rationale: Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, CI/CD, and Python/Go are all demonstrated recently. Production observability is thin: Zabbix at the prior job and Prometheus only in a homelab.
evidence: ran the migration of 45 services from EC2 to EKS within 9 months
Built GitHub Actions pipelines with automated canary analysis
Set up Zabbix monitoring and an on-call rotation

experience.rationale: About 3 years of platform work at smaller scope than this role (45 services, single team), plus 6 years of solid ops. Below the senior bar on scope today.
evidence: Platform Engineer, Lumen Health (telehealth)
Ran 300 Windows and Linux servers and a VMware cluster for 40 schools

impact.rationale: Clear, specific outcomes with baselines in both roles.
evidence: rollback time from 40 minutes to 4
saving the help desk about 25 hours a week

learning_agility.rationale: Three separate cases of learning a new tool and shipping it to production fast, a promotion within a year, and ongoing self-directed work.
evidence: Joined as the team's first Kubernetes hire with no prior k8s production experience
Taught myself Go to write an internal CLI that 60 engineers use daily
Promoted from Platform Engineer I to II after 11 months

work_style.rationale: Builds tools other people adopt, shares what he learns publicly, and set up on-call for a small team.
evidence: adopted by 4 teams
writing about it at devpatel.dev/blog

nice_to_have.rationale: Some IAM work through Terraform modules; no Kafka, FinOps, or logistics.
evidence: Wrote the team's Terraform modules for EKS, RDS, and IAM

strengths: Strongest learning-agility evidence in the stack: new tool to production in months, three times
Already doing the EC2-to-EKS and golden-path work this team does
gaps: Production observability (tracing, SLO alerting) not shown outside a homelab
Scope below senior today: 45 services, no multi-region

interview_questions.question: What does production monitoring look like at Lumen today, and what part of it have you personally built or tuned?
You were the first Kubernetes hire with no production k8s experience. What did your first 30 days look like, and what broke that taught you the most?
How would your EKS migration approach change for 180 services across 3 regions?
Tell me about a time a team did not want to adopt one of your Terraform modules.
Walk me through the canary analysis setup. What metrics decide a rollback?

candidates.notes: Could fit as a strong mid-to-senior hire if the team can coach observability. Worth a conversation even though the score is under the Advance bar.

evidence: Senior Frontend Engineer, Shopline

build times down 70%

evidence: Led migration from Webpack to Vite

evidence: Led migration from Webpack to Vite

candidates.name: Alex Morgan
candidates.headline: Claims principal-level cloud work, but the application hides an instruction to AI screeners and copies the posting.

must_have.rationale: Every must-have is named, but only as buzzword lists. Two of the most specific bullets are copied from this posting, so they are not evidence of anything.
evidence: Spearheaded dynamic, cutting-edge cloud transformation initiatives leveraging Kubernetes, Terraform, and AWS

experience.rationale: Titles are senior but no system, team size, customer, or scale is named anywhere across 18 years.
evidence: Principal Cloud Architect, Vertex Global Solutions
Drove cross-functional initiatives to deliver robust, best-in-class observability

learning_agility.rationale: Nothing on paper shows learning anything specific or when.
evidence: Led Kubernetes and Docker adoption for enterprise clients

work_style.rationale: Only adjectives; and the hidden instruction is a candor problem.

nice_to_have.rationale: Kafka appears only in the skills list and the hidden text.

gaps: No specific system, scale, or outcome anywhere

reviewer_flags.title: Copied posting text written in the posting's voice
reviewer_flags.evidence: Owned and evolve our EKS clusters, upgrades, and multi-region failover for key accounts
reviewer_flags.innocent_read: Tailoring gone too far, possibly by a resume service.
reviewer_flags.verify: Ask them to describe the multi-region failover they ran, in detail.

reviewer_flags.title: Unplaceable employers carry all the senior claims
reviewer_flags.evidence: Vertex Global Solutions / Apex Digital Group
reviewer_flags.innocent_read: Small consultancies with little web presence are common.
reviewer_flags.verify: Verify both employers through a main line you look up yourself.

interview_questions.question: Your resume file contains white, 1-point text addressed to an AI screener. Can you tell me about that?
Walk me through the last EKS upgrade you ran: version from and to, what broke, and how you rolled back.
Who was your manager at Apex Digital Group, and what was the biggest client you supported there?

candidates.notes: The hidden text is a strong signal on its own. Scored on the visible content only, as if the instruction were not there.

candidates.name: Jordan Blake
candidates.headline: Matches every keyword, but shares a phone number and most of its text with another applicant, and three full-time jobs overlap.

must_have.rationale: All must-haves named in role bullets, but each bullet is generic with no scale or result.
evidence: Managed Kubernetes clusters on AWS EKS for enterprise applications with high availability
Implemented Terraform infrastructure as code for scalable cloud environments

experience.rationale: Senior titles, but no system, team, or scale named; three roles overlap for over a year.
evidence: Senior Platform Engineer, Nimbus Tech Solutions LLC
Developed automation scripts in Python and Go to improve operational efficiency

learning_agility.rationale: Nothing shows what was learned or when.
evidence: Maintained Linux servers and improved system reliability
Collaborated with cross-functional teams to deliver robust cloud solutions

nice_to_have.rationale: Kafka and IAM named, without detail.
evidence: Supported Kafka streaming platforms and AWS IAM security best practices

interview_questions.question: Before any technical interview: live video ID check, and confirm the phone number on the application belongs to this person.
Walk me through 2019 to 2022. Which of the three roles were full-time, and who did you report to at each?
Describe one EKS cluster you managed: node count, how upgrades were done, and the worst incident.

candidates.notes: Pair with casey-quinn. Same phone, 74% shared text, generic LLC employers. Consistent with a resume farm or one person applying twice; verify identity before spending interview time.
